title: secp256k1-ecdlp: hash-indexed negation BSGS truncated at success 2/5

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x, the deterministic negation-map baby-step/giant-step algorithm in proof.md succeeds with probability at least 0.40 over the uniform challenge, by exact disjoint-window coverage, using at most 2^128.046930 total target-group-operation equivalents (batched incomplete-affine 6M additions at the fixed price C=1000 plus all other work in scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents divided by C), including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^132.675538 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^127.053161 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps or undeclared heuristics; the single declared heuristic H1 (uniform hashing for linear-probing probe counts) bounds work only and cannot change correctness or the covered set. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic generic accounting control under the current classical-group-work-v2 convention, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: On a small additive cyclic group, exhaustively check the truncated signed-window BSGS indexing: the covered set is exactly the h disjoint windows, every covered secret is recovered, and simulated linear-probing hash probes stay inside the charged budget. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
